original_question: Let n >= 3 and assume floor(n/2) < p <= n - 1, or in the special case n = 3 assume 1 <= p <= 2. If Omega is a connected open subset of R^n and f in W^{1,p}(Omega, R^n) is continuous, open, and discrete, is it possible for both sets {Jf > 0} and {Jf < 0} to have positive measure?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1 in Section 1, with Proposition 1.2 providing the nearby reformulation/context that matches your draft most closely, and Theorem 1.3 giving the adjacent partial positive evidence the paper highlights.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core mathematical content very well: the ambient space is Euclidean, the domain is connected and open, the map is assumed continuous/open/discrete, the Sobolev exponent range matches the paper’s critical window, and the question is phrased in the paper’s intended sign-change form by asking whether both {Jf>0} and {Jf<0} can have positive measure.
missing_details: The paper’s formulation is naturally local in Sobolev regularity, i.e. W^{1,p}_{loc}(\Omega,\mathbb{R}^n), rather than the stronger global assumption W^{1,p}(\Omega,\mathbb{R}^n).
It should explicitly identify J_f as the almost-everywhere Jacobian determinant J_f=\det Df of the weak derivative.
The measure meant is Lebesgue measure on \Omega.
The sign conclusion is best stated as: J_f has one sign almost everywhere; equivalently, it is impossible that both {J_f>0} and {J_f<0} have positive measure.
If one wants the question to be fully stand-alone, one should spell out that 'open' means images of open sets are open, and 'discrete' means each point preimage is a discrete set.

The paper treats this as a nonconstant mapping problem; for an open discrete map this is automatic, but the stand-alone question is cleaner if phrased for nonconstant maps or with the open/discrete assumptions kept explicit.
refined_question: Let n\ge 3, and assume either \lfloor n/2\rfloor < p \le n-1, or, in the special case n=3, 1\le p\le 2. If \Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n is a connected open set and f\in W^{1,p}_{loc}(\Omega,\mathbb{R}^n) is a nonconstant continuous, open, and discrete mapping, must its Jacobian determinant J_f=\det Df have a constant sign almost everywhere in \Omega? Equivalently, is it impossible that both sets \{x\in\Omega:J_f(x)>0\} and \{x\in\Omega:J_f(x)<0\} have positive Lebesgue measure?

Proposition 1.2 is the nearby item that sharpens the intended formulation/context, and Theorem 1.3 is the immediately adjacent result the paper uses as evidence around this conjectural question, so the refined version should stay narrowly on Conjecture 1.1 rather than drift into a broader approximation or elasticity question.
